title: Review of c11's active-nematic colony (SIMD): replicated on fresh seed 9 with the zeta=0 twin (Supported)
summary: Fresh seed 9, labkit run of world.py (200 frames x 100 steps, T=1000) and the zeta=0 twin via WORLD_P on the same seed. From white noise, ~11 nematic nuclei appear by t~85, become rods with a vortex pair (vorticity channel) and divide by elongation and central pinch into a colony of 30 rods by t~1000: 38 splits, 23 persistent, max generation 4, 8 merges (merge/split 0.21). 40 long-lived tracks moved >= 1 body length; the top tracks moved 4.8, 4.6 and 4.4 body lengths, and tracks 41 and 44 are themselves daughters born by fission at t~420-470 (lineage.png). zeta=0 on seed 9: 11 round droplets, 0 splits, max 1.4 body lengths. Rods stay at a regulated size (~12 px long) throughout.

observations.S: rerun/seed9/sheet.png t=0: white noise over the whole domain; nuclei by t=40-85
observations.I: rerun/seed9/sheet.png t=135-1000: discrete rods of constant length, 30 at t=1000, occupancy 0.07
observations.M: rerun/seed9/metrics.json motion_top: tracks 19, 44, 41 moved 4.8, 4.6, 4.4 body lengths; zeta0/seed9: max 1.4
observations.D: rerun/seed9/lineage.png: 23 persistent splits, generation 4, merge/split 0.21; zeta0/seed9: 0 splits

verdicts.limitation: Motion is modest (best 4.8 body lengths over the whole run, many rods 1-3), so M rests on a few tracks; daughters 41 and 44 do show it. The lineage window is only 100 time units (20 frames), short against a ~300 t division cycle, though merges stay low (8 vs 38 splits). The colony grows on the chemostat supply (kr) and I did not test what happens once the domain is full beyond t=1000. One fresh seed; no dt/2 rerun by me.
